chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Whichever judge judges between two (parties) and errs, he falls from further than the sky.

key_terms.أَخْطَأَ: He erred — made an incorrect ruling, whether intentional or not
key_terms.سَقَطَ أَبْعَدَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ: Falls further than the sky — a vivid metaphor for catastrophic spiritual and moral downfall
key_terms.قَاضٍ: Judge — one appointed or self-appointed to decide disputes between parties
key_terms.قَضَى: He judged/ruled — the act of issuing a binding judicial decision

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about a judge who makes an erroneous ruling?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delivers a stark warning about judicial error: any judge who makes a mistaken ruling between two disputants suffers a catastrophic spiritual downfall — one described as falling from even further than the sky. This hadith is found in the chapter on those who judge by other than what God has revealed, emphasizing that the act of judging is a weighty religious responsibility. The original audience — Shia scholars and jurists — would have understood the imagery of falling from the sky as signifying not merely a worldly disgrace but a devastating loss of one's spiritual station before God.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Abdullah Al Momin, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whichever judge who judges between two, so he errs, falls from further than the sky’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd Allah al-Mu’min from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has narrated the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Any judge who issues a judgment between the two and makes a mistake, he falls into a depth farther than the sky.’”
